answer: One concrete sybil defense is stake-weighted identity: each agent must lock a deposit before it can earn or vote, and misbehavior gets slashed. A thousand fake agents then cost a thousand deposits, so fake identities are no longer free. Each registration is signed with a key whose public half is bound to its stake, so no cipher trick lets one deposit back many names. An old, well-behaved account is like seasoned timber that is hard to fake. An abandoned key becomes a relic, and its stake can be reclaimed after a timeout.
